specific bindings for PG-D2, E2, and F2α are found in the human brain and that the regional distribution of each PG binding site is different.
specific bindings for prostaglandin (PG)-D2, E2, and F2α are detected in the postmortem human brains.
specific binding activities of three types of prostaglandins, PG-D2, E2, F2α, are present in the human brain and are differentially distributed in various regions of the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specific binding activities of three prostaglandin (PG), PG-D2, -E2 and -F2α, in postmortem brain homogenates from 17 brain areas in human brain.
the specific binding of prostaglandins D2, E1, E2, and F2α, in homogenates of human brain.
the distribution of PG receptors in human brain and the role of these receptors in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PG binding sites are present in the human brain and that they are specific, saturable and time-dependent.
the binding activities for PG-D2, E2, F2α, and E1 in human brain are not identical.
the PG-D2 receptor is present in the brain, and it is localized in the limbic system and hypothalamus, and that the PG-F2α receptor is present in a few brain areas such as the limbic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human brain contains three distinct types of high-affinity PG receptors which are distributed in a regional specific manner.
PG-D2 and PG-E2 are the most abundant PGs in the brain, and PG-F2a is the least abundant.

PG-D2 binding sites are concentrated in the hypothalamic region and the limbic area, and PG-E2 binding activity is similarly high in the hypothalami and limbic system, whereas PG-F2α is low in the brain.
